result.summary: The CPU scheduler picks the next ready process to run. Preemptive scheduling can take the CPU from a running process. FCFS runs processes in arrival order but suffers the convoy effect. SJF runs the smallest next CPU burst for minimum average waiting time, but needs burst prediction and can starve long processes. Round Robin gives each process a fixed time quantum, then moves it to the back of the queue; a very large quantum acts like FCFS. Priority scheduling runs the highest-priority process first, and aging fixes starvation. Metrics are turnaround, waiting and response time.

result.summary: Time complexity describes how running time grows with input size n, not exact seconds. Big-O gives an upper bound: f(n) is O(g(n)) if constants c and n0 exist with f(n) <= c*g(n) for all n >= n0. Common classes run from O(1) and O(log n) up to O(n^2) and O(2^n). Constants and lower-order terms are dropped. Binary search is O(log n) and linear search is O(n). Big-Omega gives a lower bound and Big-Theta a tight bound. Space complexity measures extra memory as a function of n.

result.summary: Normalization organizes tables to reduce redundancy and avoid update, insertion and deletion anomalies. A functional dependency X -> Y means each value of X determines exactly one value of Y. First Normal Form (1NF) requires atomic values and no repeating groups. Second Normal Form (2NF) forbids partial dependency on a composite primary key. Third Normal Form (3NF) forbids transitive dependency between non-key attributes. BCNF is stricter: for every functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a superkey. Denormalization deliberately adds redundancy back to speed up reads, at the cost of more complex updates.

result.summary: TCP is a connection-oriented, reliable, byte-stream transport protocol that retransmits lost segments. A connection is established with a three-way handshake and closed with a four-way teardown. Sequence numbers label bytes so the receiver can reorder segments and detect loss, and ACKs confirm receipt. Flow control uses the receiver's advertised window (rwnd). Congestion control starts with slow start, which roughly doubles cwnd each round trip until ssthresh, then congestion avoidance adds about one segment per round trip. On a timeout, ssthresh is set to half of cwnd and slow start restarts. UDP, by contrast, is connectionless and gives no delivery guarantee.

result.summary: Gradient descent minimises a loss function L(w) by repeatedly moving parameters w opposite to the gradient. A learning rate that is too small converges slowly; one that is too large can overshoot and diverge. Batch gradient descent uses the whole training set: stable but slow for large data. Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) uses one example per update: fast and noisy, which can help escape shallow local minima. Mini-batch gradient descent, with a small batch, is the usual choice in practice. On convex losses such as mean squared error, a suitable learning rate reaches the global minimum. Feature scaling speeds up convergence, and an epoch is one full pass through the training data.

result.summary: A prompt is the input given to a language model, and output quality depends strongly on how it is written. Zero-shot prompting gives an instruction with no examples; few-shot prompting adds input-output examples so the model can imitate the pattern and format. A good prompt states the role, task, context, constraints and required output format. Chain-of-thought prompting asks for step-by-step reasoning, which often helps arithmetic and logic. Hallucination is fluent but unsupported or false content; grounding the model in provided documents and asking for quoted sources reduces it. Temperature controls randomness: low gives more deterministic output, high more varied output. Prompt injection occurs when untrusted text tries to override developer instructions. Prompts should be tested on a fixed test set and versioned like code.

result.summary: The MMU translates logical addresses, and base and limit registers enforce protection. Contiguous allocation causes fragmentation; paging avoids external fragmentation with frames, pages and a page table, cached by a TLB. Multi-level page tables and segmentation handle large tables and logical units. Virtual memory and demand paging load pages only when needed, and page replacement chooses a victim when no frame is free. FIFO, optimal and LRU are replacement algorithms; FIFO can show Belady's anomaly, while LRU does not. Thrashing occurs when a process lacks frames, and the working-set model or fault-rate control can allocate them.

key_terms.evidence: A program generates logical addresses (also called virtual addresses).

key_terms.definition: The hardware that translates logical addresses into physical addresses in main memory.
key_terms.evidence: The hardware that translates them into physical addresses in main memory is the memory management unit (MMU).

key_terms.definition: A free block of memory in contiguous allocation.
key_terms.evidence: Free blocks are called holes.

key_terms.definition: A situation where enough total free memory exists for a request but it is split into holes that are too small.
key_terms.evidence: External fragmentation means there is enough total free memory for a request, but it is split into holes that are too small.

key_terms.definition: Wasted space inside an allocated block that is larger than the memory requested.
key_terms.evidence: Internal fragmentation means memory allocated to a process is larger than requested, so the unused space inside the block is wasted.

key_terms.definition: A fixed-size block of physical memory.
key_terms.evidence: Physical memory is divided into fixed-size blocks called frames

key_terms.definition: A table that maps each page number to a frame number.
key_terms.evidence: A page table maps each page number to a frame number.

key_terms.definition: A small, fast hardware cache of page table entries.
key_terms.evidence: The translation look-aside buffer (TLB) is a small, fast hardware cache of page table entries.

key_terms.definition: A scheme that views memory as logical units such as the code, stack and heap, using a segment table of base and limit values.

key_terms.definition: Loading a page into memory only when it is needed.

key_terms.definition: An event that happens when a process references a page that is not in memory.
key_terms.evidence: A page fault happens when a process references a page that is not in memory.

key_terms.definition: A state where a process lacks enough frames for its active pages, so it spends more time paging than executing.

questions.evidence: Paging has no external fragmentation, but it can have internal fragmentation in the last page of a process.

result.summary: The software development life cycle has requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment and maintenance. The waterfall model runs phases in sequence, suiting stable requirements, while agile delivers working software in short iterations with customer feedback. Scrum has a Product Owner, Scrum Master and Development Team, uses a product backlog, sprint backlog and increment, and holds sprints with planning, daily scrums, reviews and retrospectives. Testing spans unit, integration, system and acceptance levels, plus black-box, white-box and regression techniques. Version control, code review, continuous integration and delivery support frequent, tested changes, and technical debt is reduced by refactoring.
